raw_findings.body: Every spec-conformant browser report fails validation and the endpoint returns 422, so the collector rejects the exact traffic it was built to gather; no metrics are recorded for real reports.
raw_findings.failure_mode: All genuine browser reports are rejected with HTTP 422, defeating the data-collection purpose of the endpoint.
raw_findings.impact: Every spec-conformant browser report fails validation and the endpoint returns 422, so the collector rejects the exact traffic it was built to gather; no metrics are recorded for real reports.
raw_findings.root_cause: The new serializer treats spec-internal report fields as required request fields, conflating the report concept model with the delivered JSON serialization.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Mark `destination` and `attempts` as `required=False` (or drop them from the serializer) so wire-format reports validate.
raw_findings.title: Serializer requires `destination`/`attempts` fields that browsers do not send in the Reporting API wire format
raw_findings.trigger: A real browser POSTs reports to the collector. Per both the W3C Working Draft and Editor's Draft, serialized reports delivered over the wire contain only `age` (or `timestamp`), `type`, `url`, `user_agent`, and `body`; `destination` and `attempts` are internal report-concept fields never included in the POST payload.

raw_findings.body: The intended "exactly one of age/timestamp" invariant is silently not enforced when the other field is 0, so contradictory payloads pass validation and downstream consumers cannot rely on the exclusivity guarantee.
raw_findings.evidence:
if self.initial_data.get("age"):
            raise serializers.ValidationError("If timestamp is present, age must be absent")
raw_findings.failure_mode: Validation accepts payloads containing both `age` and `timestamp` whenever one of them is falsy, violating the documented cross-field rule.
raw_findings.impact: The intended "exactly one of age/timestamp" invariant is silently not enforced when the other field is 0, so contradictory payloads pass validation and downstream consumers cannot rely on the exclusivity guarantee.
raw_findings.root_cause: `initial_data.get(...)` truthiness is used to test field presence, which treats the valid value 0 as absent.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Check key presence explicitly, e.g. `if "age" in self.initial_data:` (and the mirror check in `validate_age`), instead of truthiness.
raw_findings.title: Truthiness-based mutual-exclusion checks let `age=0` or `timestamp=0` bypass the age/timestamp exclusivity rule
raw_findings.trigger: A report submits both fields where one is zero, e.g. `{"age": 0, "timestamp": 1234}` — `age` of 0 is a legitimate value meaning the report was generated just now.

raw_findings.body: Reports lacking any timing information validate successfully and are counted as valid reports, contradicting both specs (each requires one of the two fields) and the serializer's own comments about supporting them.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Invalid time-less reports are accepted instead of being rejected with 422.
raw_findings.impact: Reports lacking any timing information validate successfully and are counted as valid reports, contradicting both specs (each requires one of the two fields) and the serializer's own comments about supporting them.
raw_findings.root_cause: The serializer models the two spec variants as independently optional fields without an at-least-one-of constraint.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Add a `validate()` method that raises a ValidationError when both `age` and `timestamp` are absent.
raw_findings.title: Neither `age` nor `timestamp` is required, so reports with no time field pass validation
raw_findings.trigger: A malformed report omits both `age` and `timestamp`; the cross-field validators only fire when one of the fields is present, so nothing enforces that at least one exists.

raw_findings.body: The seconds-based error timestamp is always smaller than the milliseconds-based event timestamp, so every error message is emitted before all breadcrumb messages instead of being interleaved chronologically, and the raw timestamps in the generated log lines use inconsistent units, degrading the Seer summary quality.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Chronological ordering of the combined error/breadcrumb log is wrong for essentially every replay with errors.
raw_findings.impact: The seconds-based error timestamp is always smaller than the milliseconds-based event timestamp, so every error message is emitted before all breadcrumb messages instead of being interleaved chronologically, and the raw timestamps in the generated log lines use inconsistent units, degrading the Seer summary quality.
raw_findings.root_cause: New merge logic compares timestamps from two sources without converting between seconds and milliseconds epochs.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Normalize units before comparison (e.g., multiply error timestamps by 1000 or divide event timestamps by 1000) and emit a consistent unit in the log messages.
raw_findings.title: Error timestamps (seconds) compared against rrweb event timestamps (milliseconds) breaks chronological interleaving
raw_findings.trigger: Any replay with associated errors is summarized: error timestamps fetched from nodestore are unix-epoch seconds (~1.7e9), while rrweb replay event `timestamp` values are epoch milliseconds (~1.7e12).

raw_findings.body: If the returned dict order diverges from `error_ids` order, each ErrorEvent gets the wrong `id` paired with another event's title/message/timestamp, producing incorrect error context in the summary.
raw_findings.evidence: for event_id, data in zip(error_ids, events.values())
raw_findings.failure_mode: Error IDs can be silently associated with the wrong event payloads, corrupting the error details fed to Seer.
raw_findings.impact: If the returned dict order diverges from `error_ids` order, each ErrorEvent gets the wrong `id` paired with another event's title/message/timestamp, producing incorrect error context in the summary.
raw_findings.root_cause: Positional pairing of request ids with dict values relies on an unguaranteed ordering contract of `get_multi`.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Look up each node id explicitly, e.g. iterate `for error_id, node_id in zip(error_ids, node_ids)` and fetch `events.get(node_id)`, instead of relying on `events.values()` ordering.
raw_findings.title: `zip(error_ids, events.values())` assumes nodestore get_multi returns values in request order
raw_findings.trigger: `nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids)` returns a dict keyed by node id; backends (especially cached/wrapped implementations that merge cache hits with backend fetches) do not guarantee the dict's insertion order matches the input `node_ids` order.

raw_findings.body: `process_raw_response` filters the response to the requested fields, so `response[0].get("error_ids", [])` returns empty and error context is silently dropped from the summary even though `enable_error_context` is true.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Error context silently disappears from summaries depending on unrelated query parameters supplied by the client.
raw_findings.impact: `process_raw_response` filters the response to the requested fields, so `response[0].get("error_ids", [])` returns empty and error context is silently dropped from the summary even though `enable_error_context` is true.
raw_findings.root_cause: The internal replay-instance lookup reuses the caller's `field` query parameters for a response the endpoint consumes itself.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Pass a fixed field list (e.g. `fields=["error_ids"]`) to `process_raw_response` since this endpoint only needs error IDs, rather than forwarding user-controlled query params.
raw_findings.title: `error_ids` extraction depends on user-supplied `field` query params instead of a fixed field list
raw_findings.trigger: A client calls the summarize endpoint with any `?field=...` query parameter that does not include `error_ids` (e.g. `?field=id`).

raw_findings.body: Rendered comments contain a blank line between every list item (double newline) and a stray trailing newline before the footer, changing the Markdown list from a tight list to a loose list and degrading comment formatting versus the previous template which had no trailing newline.
raw_findings.failure_mode: PR/MR comments render with extra blank lines between suspect-issue bullets.
raw_findings.impact: Rendered comments contain a blank line between every list item (double newline) and a stray trailing newline before the footer, changing the Markdown list from a tight list to a loose list and degrading comment formatting versus the previous template which had no trailing newline.
raw_findings.root_cause: The new shared template embeds a line terminator while the existing call sites still join items with an explicit newline.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Remove the trailing "\n" from the template and keep relying on the "\n".join in the callers.
raw_findings.title: Trailing newline in MERGED_PR_SINGLE_ISSUE_TEMPLATE combined with '\n'.join produces blank lines between issue bullets
raw_findings.trigger: Any merged-PR comment with more than one suspect issue: `get_comment_body` in the GitHub/GitLab workflows joins the formatted templates with "\n", and each template already ends in "\n".

Additionally, the flag string is not registered in src/sentry/features, so the branch is unreachable dead code until registration, hiding the regression from tests.

                },

raw_findings.failure_mode: Users behind the feature flag see blank dashboard tables while the underlying query returns valid data.
raw_findings.impact: Every table widget renders an empty table (no columns, no rows) instead of the fetched `result.data`/`result.meta`, silently discarding real query results. The in-scope `result`, `fields`, and `fieldAliases` are never passed to the new component. Additionally, the flag string is not registered in src/sentry/features, so the branch is unreachable dead code until registration, hiding the regression from tests.
raw_findings.root_cause: The new feature-flag branch was added with placeholder empty `columns` and `tableData` props instead of mapping the existing `result`/`fields` values.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Wire actual data into the new component: pass `tableData={{data: result.data, meta: result.meta}}` (adapted to TabularData) and derive `columns` from `fields`/`fieldAliases`, or remove the branch until the integration is implemented; also register the feature flag if the branch is intended to ship.
raw_findings.title: Feature-flagged TableWidgetVisualization renders hardcoded empty data instead of widget query results
raw_findings.trigger: An organization with the 'use-table-widget-visualization' feature flag enabled views a dashboard containing a table-type widget; tableResultComponent renders the new branch.

raw_findings.body: The deleted `FlexCenter` styled component applied `${p => p.theme.overflowEllipsis}` (overflow: hidden) to the cell, which allowed the 1fr grid track to shrink and the name to truncate. The replacement `<Flex align="center">` has `overflow: visible`, so the grid item's automatic minimum size is content-based and long names can blow out the first column, breaking the table layout instead of ellipsizing.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Visual regression: attachment rows with long file names overflow or distort the panel table columns.
raw_findings.impact: The deleted `FlexCenter` styled component applied `${p => p.theme.overflowEllipsis}` (overflow: hidden) to the cell, which allowed the 1fr grid track to shrink and the name to truncate. The replacement `<Flex align="center">` has `overflow: visible`, so the grid item's automatic minimum size is content-based and long names can blow out the first column, breaking the table layout instead of ellipsizing.

finding.body: Every spec-conformant browser report fails validation and the endpoint returns 422, so the collector rejects the exact traffic it was built to gather; no metrics are recorded for real reports.

finding.root_cause: The new serializer treats spec-internal report fields as required request fields, conflating the report concept model with the delivered JSON serialization.
finding.suggested_fix: Mark `destination` and `attempts` as `required=False` (or drop them from the serializer) so wire-format reports validate.
finding.title: Serializer requires `destination`/`attempts` fields that browsers do not send in the Reporting API wire format
finding.trigger: A real browser POSTs reports to the collector. Per both the W3C Working Draft and Editor's Draft, serialized reports delivered over the wire contain only `age` (or `timestamp`), `type`, `url`, `user_agent`, and `body`; `destination` and `attempts` are internal report-concept fields never included in the POST payload.

The W3C Reporting API Working Draft (https://www.w3.org/TR/reporting-1/) specifies these fields in the report concept. The serializer is implementing the spec as documented in the code comments. Without external spec verification showing these fields are truly internal-only, this is ungrounded speculation.

validated_findings.body: Every spec-conformant browser report fails validation and the endpoint returns 422, so the collector rejects the exact traffic it was built to gather; no metrics are recorded for real reports.

validated_findings.root_cause: The new serializer treats spec-internal report fields as required request fields, conflating the report concept model with the delivered JSON serialization.

validated_findings.title: Serializer requires `destination`/`attempts` fields that browsers do not send in the Reporting API wire format
validated_findings.trigger: A real browser POSTs reports to the collector. Per both the W3C Working Draft and Editor's Draft, serialized reports delivered over the wire contain only `age` (or `timestamp`), `type`, `url`, `user_agent`, and `body`; `destination` and `attempts` are internal report-concept fields never included in the POST payload.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: The claim that browsers never send `destination` and `attempts` is incorrect. The W3C Reporting API Working Draft (https://www.w3.org/TR/reporting-1/) specifies these fields in the report concept. The serializer is implementing the spec as documented in the code comments. Without external spec verification showing these fields are truly internal-only, this is ungrounded speculation.

validated_findings.body: The removed `FlexContainer` used `flex: 1`, which expands to `flex-grow: 1; flex-shrink: 1; flex-basis: 0%`. `Flex.Item grow={1}` renders `flex-grow: 1; flex-shrink: 1; flex-basis: auto` (per flex.tsx, basis defaults to 'auto'). With `flex-basis: auto` the item's hypothetical size is its content size instead of 0, so wide description content now competes with and can squeeze the Metadata column, changing the layout compared to before the refactor.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Visual layout regression: description column no longer sized from a zero basis, allowing content-driven widths to push the Metadata sidebar.
validated_findings.impact: The removed `FlexContainer` used `flex: 1`, which expands to `flex-grow: 1; flex-shrink: 1; flex-basis: 0%`. `Flex.Item grow={1}` renders `flex-grow: 1; flex-shrink: 1; flex-basis: auto` (per flex.tsx, basis defaults to 'auto'). With `flex-basis: auto` the item's hypothetical size is its content size instead of 0, so wide description content now competes with and can squeeze the Metadata column, changing the layout compared to before the refactor.
validated_findings.root_cause: Refactor replaced a `flex: 1` shorthand with a `flex-grow: 1` longhand, silently changing flex-basis from 0% to auto.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Use `<Flex.Item flex={1}>` (which emits `flex: 1` and thus `flex-basis: 0%`) instead of `grow={1}` to preserve the previous layout behavior.
validated_findings.title: Flex.Item grow={1} is not equivalent to removed `flex: 1` (flex-basis auto vs 0%)
validated_findings.trigger: Rendering the integration information card when the Description/FeatureList content is wide (long markdown, long feature descriptions) next to the Metadata sidebar.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: The patch shows `<FlexContainer>` (which had `flex: 1`) replaced with `<Flex.Item grow={1}>`. Repository context confirms Flex.Item with grow={1} renders `flex-grow: 1; flex-shrink: 1; flex-basis: auto` (flex.tsx L35-46), while `flex: 1` expands to `flex-basis: 0%`. This is a semantic difference that could cause layout changes with wide content.

validated_findings.body: Introduces a deprecated typing alias (deprecated since Python 3.9 per PEP 585) and an inconsistent annotation style within the same test, adding an unnecessary typing import that linters/pyupgrade will flag and future maintainers must clean up.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Style/convention regression: deprecated typing alias and inconsistent generic annotation style are introduced into a file that otherwise uses PEP 585 builtin generics.
validated_findings.impact: Introduces a deprecated typing alias (deprecated since Python 3.9 per PEP 585) and an inconsistent annotation style within the same test, adding an unnecessary typing import that linters/pyupgrade will flag and future maintainers must clean up.
validated_findings.root_cause: The new test uses the legacy `typing.DefaultDict` alias instead of the builtin generic `defaultdict[str, int]` already enabled by `from __future__ import annotations` and used throughout the patch/file.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Annotate as `expected_message_counts_dict: defaultdict[str, int] = defaultdict(int)` and drop `DefaultDict` from the typing import on line 6.
validated_findings.title: Deprecated typing.DefaultDict used inconsistently with builtin generics in the same patch
validated_findings.trigger: Any reviewer or type-checker reading the new test: the file already has `from __future__ import annotations` and the same patch annotates with PEP 585 builtin generics (`list[tuple[str, int]]` on the adjacent line and `dict[str, Any]` elsewhere in the module), yet this line and the new `from typing import Any, DefaultDict, TypedDict` import introduce the deprecated `typing.DefaultDict` alias.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: This is a style issue about using `typing.DefaultDict` vs builtin `defaultdict[str, int]`. The code functions correctly. While PEP 585 deprecates typing aliases, this is a minor style inconsistency that doesn't affect runtime behavior or correctness. Style issues are explicitly excluded from valid findings.
